lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: volume of cylinders cones and spheres

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 3.

steps: Identify the quantities and the applicable model.
Check that the result answers the question.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A cylinder and cone each have radius 2 units and height 18 units. Which has the greater volume?
As x increases, y generally increases. What association does this scatter plot describe?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Most plotted points follow y = 2x + 1. Of these points, (11, 23), (12, 25), (10, 21), (11, 35), which point is an outlier?
A line of fit is y = 4x + 6. Predict y when x = 10.
A data set has x-values from 4 through 16. A prediction is made at x = 18. Is this interpolation or extrapolation?
A line of fit is y = 5x + 10. Predict y when x = 6.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: Umbrella sales and rainy-day traffic delays are correlated. Which conclusion is justified?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Find the exact volume of a cylinder with radius 5 units and height 12 units. Express your answer as a rational multiple of π.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
